messages.content: Write the introduction to a public product roadmap for a developer tools company. Around 200 words.

output:
**Roadmap**

Here's what we're building, and roughly when.

We publish this for one reason: you're making decisions about your stack that depend on ours. If something you need is six months out, you deserve to know that now, while you can still route around it.

A few rules for reading it. "Shipping" means the work is in progress and we'd be surprised to miss the quarter. "Planned" means we've committed engineers but not dates. "Exploring" means we're still arguing about it internally — treat those as open questions, not promises. Anything not on this page isn't secretly in flight somewhere.

We reorder this constantly. Last quarter we pulled the SAML work forward by three months because forty-odd teams asked for it inside the same six weeks, and pushed the plugin API back because our first design didn't survive contact with the beta group. That will happen again. When it does, we'll say so in the changelog instead of quietly editing the page.

The fastest way to move something up the list is to tell us what you're blocked on, in the discussion thread linked beside each item. Specific beats loud.

---

~205 words. The SAML/plugin-API details are placeholders — swap in a real reordering you've done, since that paragraph is the one doing the credibility work.
